game: JAX @ SF, 2025-09-28 16:05 ET, SF -3.5, total 45.5, outdoor, weather forecast not saved

script.base: SF is a 3.5-point home favorite with implied totals SF 24.5 and JAX 21.0 in a mid total (45.5), so this is a one-score game, not a blowout and not a shootout. SF leads late and closes with Christian McCaffrey (52 carries and 32 targets over weeks 1-3). JAX stays live enough to throw, but Travis Etienne (46 carries, 270 yards) does not get a clock-killing spike against a front that has allowed 3.70 YPC.
script.flip1: SF jumps up by two scores. Purdy and the questionable WRs stall late, McCaffrey runs the clock, and JAX abandons the run, so Etienne's rush line dies while Brian Thomas Jr. (25 targets), Brenton Strange (16) and Parker Washington (16) see catch-up targets.
script.flip2: JAX hangs around or leads, so Lawrence stays balanced, Etienne keeps 15-plus carries and can clear 71.5 on one crease, and SF cannot just hand it to McCaffrey. A weather slog is the other version of this flip, but no forecast was saved, so it cannot be used.

injury_fallout: Official pre-game report: JAX G Wyatt Milum is out (knee), so rush efficiency should fall and quick throws should rise toward Strange (16 targets, 137 yards, 108 air) and Etienne's checkdowns (8 targets, 31 yards, -30 air). JAX LB Yasir Abdullah is out (hamstring), which helps SF's middle targets (McCaffrey 32 targets/213 yards, Jake Tonges 11/67) more than it helps a JAX rusher. JAX WR Dyami Brown is questionable (shoulder; 14 targets, 116 yards, 162 air); if he sits, Washington (16/110/170) and Travis Hunter (16/76/105) absorb looks, but he is not out. SF WR Jordan Watkins is out (calf) with zero targets in the weeks 1-3 log, so no redistribution. SF WR Ricky Pearsall (24 targets, 281 yards, 398 air) and Jauan Jennings (15/105) are both questionable, as are CB Renardo Green (neck), G Connor Colby (groin) and backup QB Mac Jones (knee). Mac Jones does not change the starter (Brock Purdy has the 3 SF QB rushes in the log). If Pearsall or Jennings is limited, McCaffrey and Tonges gain targets; if Green sits, the JAX outside-WR case changes and is unnamed. SF DT C.J. West is out (thumb), a small give-back to the JAX run. No practice grades (DNP/limited/full) and no 90-minute inactives are in the pack. Sources: nflverse pre-game injury report and weeks 1-3 carry/target logs in the pack.

Abdullah out and JAX's 6.48 middle YPA overlap McCaffrey/Tonges; JAX's 4.24 YPC overlaps McCaffrey's carries. No primary corner is named in the pack.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Etienne's 71.5 rush line is his median, but SF has allowed 3.70 YPC and only 4 runs of 10+, he is the 3.5-point dog so the script throws more, and Milum is out, so a full regression toward that front lands nearer 55 than 71.5.
edge_players.must_be_true: Etienne keeps the lead role (46 carries vs Tuten 17 and Bigsby 5), SF stays near 3.70 YPC, Milum remains out, and JAX does not control the clock.
edge_players.kills_it: JAX leads and he gets 18-plus carries, he breaks another long run like the 143-yard game (SF has allowed 4 runs of 10+), or West's absence plus only a partial YPC regression (around 4.5 on 16 carries) pushes him through 71.5. Tagged script-dependent on the JAX-lead flip.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and Etienne under 71.5 lost because the one-score game never forced JAX off the run: he got 18-20 carries, broke one 15-plus run against a front that has already allowed 4 runs of 10+, and C.J. West's absence kept YPC closer to the mid-4s than to 3.70. Tuten (17 carries, 74 yards, one 42-yard game) did not steal the explosive. The 90-yard mean was the warning, and the flag said not to size it. Milum's absence was either already in the number or did not show up in the interior fit.

The correlated favorite-runs-the-clock partner would have been McCaffrey rush over 55.5, but that lean was dropped when the 69/55/52 trend disagreed.
